items.name: Eynap
items.tagline: Everything You Need as an AI PM
items.summary: An AI PM skill kit: one orchestrator that routes by stage, six skills from research to PRD, and one shared foundation every skill reads.
items.details:
## What it is

Research, framing, PRD, entity state machines, design handoff — each written down in a form an AI can read, so an agent can carry a PM's work. One orchestrator decides the stage, routes to a skill and checks the gate; the skills cover value, flow, entity, design, PRD and research; and a shared foundation holds memory, preferences, naming, protocols, host differences and wording rules.

Call the one you need directly — no need to run the whole pipeline.

## The chain

Building a product from scratch, the skills run **value → flow → entity → design → prd**. The PRD comes last because its journey, entity and interaction chapters *are* those outputs. Research is called on demand, not run first.

## Credits

An adaptation of [SmileLiuuuu/ai-pm](https://github.com/SmileLiuuuu/ai-pm), released under the same CC BY-NC 4.0 license. The methodology comes from v1; v3 splits it into independently callable skills.
items.installNote: Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and 70+ other hosts. You can also paste the line to your AI and let it install itself.

items.name: /devloop
items.summary: autonomous unattended dev loop — branch → small step → test → PR → sub-agent review → merge → verify deploy → next
items.details:
## What it does

A self-paced loop that works through a queue of issues, one at a time:
branch → small implementation steps → test hard → PR → an independent sub-agent
code-reviews → merge → verify the deploy → update the issue → next.

## Why I built it

Hand-running every PR is hours of attention I'd rather spend on product
strategy. The loop turns my backlog into something I can hand off and check
the next morning.

## How it works

- Self-paced via `ScheduleWakeup` between steps — no fixed cadence, picks the next interval based on what's being waited on
- Each PR gets reviewed by a fresh sub-agent (no rubber-stamping)
- Pages deploy is verified before marking the issue done
- Stops cleanly when the queue is empty

## Best result so far

Cleared 8 issues on this very site overnight, one PAT, fully unattended.

## Stack

Claude Code skill at `~/.claude/skills/devloop/`. Reusable across any git repo.
items.tagline: An unattended dev loop that works your issue queue
items.installNote: Then run /devloop in Claude Code. Per project instead of global: put it in <repo>/.claude/skills/devloop/.

items.name: /ai-pm-resume
items.summary: AI PM résumé reviewer — 8-dim signal audit + 5-reader critique + anti-fab guardrails + tier adaptation
items.details:
## What it does

Reviews and rewrites a résumé specifically for AI PM roles. Runs:

- An **8-dimension AI-PM signal audit** (model fluency, eval craft, agent reasoning, infra literacy, taste, shipping cadence, …)
- A **5-reader critique** — the same résumé read by an ATS bot, a hiring manager, an AI engineer, a peer AI PM, and a recruiter; each with their own rubric
- A bullet **rewriter with anti-fabrication guardrails**
- **Tier adaptation** — big tech / AI startup / 中国大厂（字节飞书）/ 应届

## Why I built it

Generic résumé "optimizers" don't know what an AI engineer looks for in a PM
bullet (vs what a recruiter scans for). I wanted one tool that splits the
signal by reader role and refuses to invent metrics.

## Anti-fab rule

The skill will not insert numbers, durations, team sizes, or names that
aren't in the source. If you give it `built X`, you get `built X` — not
`built X in 6 months with a 4-person team`.

## Stack

Claude Code skill at `~/.claude/skills/ai-pm-resume/`.
items.tagline: A résumé reviewer that reads like an AI PM hiring loop
items.installNote: Or fetch just SKILL.md into ~/.claude/skills/ai-pm-resume/. Then ask Claude Code to review your résumé for an AI PM role.

checks: 8-dimension AI-PM signal audit, each dimension scored 0–3 with bullet-level evidence
5-reader critique: ATS bot, hiring manager, AI engineer, peer AI PM, recruiter
Anti-fabrication checkpoints on numbers, attribution, status and verbs

items.name: /interview-sim
items.summary: synthetic interview generator — protocol + persona → time-budgeted transcript that reads like recording transcription, not LLM output
items.details:
## What it does

Takes an **interview protocol** + a **受访者画像** (real person or fictional persona) and produces a **transcript that reads like a real recording transcription**, not an LLM Q&A. The bar isn't "answer well" — it's **"sound like that person"**: hits their knowledge edges, gets stuck, self-corrects, asks the interviewer back, occasionally goes off-topic.

## Use cases

- **UX research synthetic interviews** — HCDE / product research, protocol + user persona → a transcript you can code
- **Expert / journalist-style interviews** of public figures (research-backed, not invented)
- **Mock interviews — interviewee side** — you write the questions, the agent plays the candidate
- Any context that wants a plausible interview transcript as research / writing material

## How it works

- **Kickoff intake-clarify** — an `AskUserQuestion` round to align on protocol / persona / duration / language / setting / disfluency level / interviewer style / how strictly to stay in character — *before* it goes off researching
- **Real persona** → parallel `WebSearch` + `WebFetch` across LinkedIn / podcasts / talks / articles / posts; builds a dossier that strictly separates **verified** vs **inferred** facts
- **Fictional persona** → cohort-representative research: searches for how this kind of person actually talks, anchors the synthesis in real-world data, refuses to invent from thin air
- **Duration calibration** — English ≈150 wpm, Chinese ≈220 字/min, Japanese ≈300 字/min; word-count budget allocated across questions by weight
- **High-realism disfluency toolbox** — bilingual filler / self-correction / questioning-back / pause templates, **clustered at thought transitions** (not sprinkled evenly — that's caricature, not realism)
- **Real-respondent cognitive patterns** — struggling to find words, talking around the question, hedging, stated-vs-actual mismatches, admitting they don't know — at least 1–2 visible cognitive struggles per session
- **Anti-fabrication red lines** — no inventing biographical facts for real people, no quietly upgrading a fictional persona mid-interview, no fabricated numbers / quotes ever
- **Interviewer half-structured probing** — protocol's main questions + natural follow-ups ("can you say more about that", "can you give a specific example"), **never leading questions**
- **Output dual channel** — saves `interview_<persona-slug>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` AND prints the full transcript inline
- **Self-check before delivery** — 8-item checklist (identity drift, cognitive struggle, filler distribution, leading Qs, biographical sourcing, fabricated numbers, word-count drift, language consistency)

## Why I built it

UX-research synthetic interviews are everywhere now, but most of them read like LLM Q&A — the fictional user is suspiciously articulate, never stuck, never wrong, and the dialogue feels written. That's useless as research material. This skill bakes in disfluency, knowledge edges, and anti-fabrication so the transcript is plausible enough to actually code.

## Stack

Claude Code skill. Install: `git clone https://github.com/AntaresYuan/claude-skill-interview-sim ~/.claude/skills/interview-sim`
